newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy centre-right wins Milan, loses Turin, Trieste.
newsitem.headline: Italy centre-right wins Milan, loses Turin, Trieste.

text.p: The centre-right oppostion bloc triumphed in a mayoral election in Milan but lost in Turin and Trieste to the centre-left parties that back the ruling national coalition.
The three big northern cities were seen as the key prizes in the second round of local elections for 77 mayors and five provincial presidents on Sunday.

Final results in Milan showed that the candidate backed by the Freedom Alliance candidate, industrialist Gabriele Albertini, secured 53.1 percent of the vote while his rival Aldo Fumagalli of the centre-left won 46.9 percent.

In neighbouring Turin, home of car giant Fiat, centre-left candidate Valentino Castellani beat the centre-right's Raffaele Costa by a hair, winning 50.4 percent of the vote to 49.6 percent for his rival.
In northeastern Trieste, Riccardo Illy of the centre-left cruised home with 53.9 percent against 46.1 percent for Adalberto Donaggio.

In the seven other of the 10 largest cities cities where voting was held, the centre-left won two, Ancona and Novara, the centre-right won Catanzaro and Crotone, and looked certain to win with a wide margin in Terni.
The separatist Northern League won Lecco and Pordenone.
